accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE Relationships Education statutory guidance (2019), Respectful relationships, which lists the responsibilities of bystanders (primarily reporting bullying to an adult) and how to get help; the IB PYP PSPE interactions strand codes PSPE.INT.P1.CU.5 and P2.LO.11 attached to this topic; Hawkins, Pepler and Craig (2001), peers present in most playground bullying episodes and peer interventions often stopping it within 10 seconds; and Darley and Latane (1968) on diffusion of responsibility. No advice tells a child to step in physically; every high-risk scene resolves to fetching an adult.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips in anti-bullying work: that doing nothing is neutral (Ola prediction and the bystander-in-Upstander sorter message), that laughing, cheering or filming is just watching (Ivy and Sam cards, crowd step), that a big crowd guarantees help (Be the first prediction and challenge tag cared), that upstanding means fighting or being mean back (Be mean back tile, push and alone challenge tags) and that reporting is telling tales (telling step prediction, tales and business tags).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagupst is about the bystander choice itself: a three-way participant-role sorter (joins in, bystander, upstander), an audience bar that falls only as watchers stop laughing, a crowd of six where one first helper triggers the rest, a risk-rated scene that only accepts the safe move for its risk level, and a reporting versus telling-tales sort. flagbully (repetition, intent, power, bullying types) and flagcare share none of these mechanisms; the 30% shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each task makes the child act out the idea before the text names it: Ola cannot go in Upstander, the audience bar only empties when all four laughing children stop, the other five children only change their thought to I will help after one is tapped, the pushing scene rejects Speak up and Stand with and accepts only Tell a grown-up, and the lunch card refuses Telling tales. Done messages then state the rule (No audience, no show; Big risk: get a grown-up).

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, she did nothing mean' for Ola, 'Nothing changes' when watchers stop laughing, 'Yes, with so many, someone will' for the crowd, and 'Yes, it is snitching' for telling a teacher. Each task straight after disproves the wrong pick and A.reveal quotes the child's guess.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with tagged wrong answers and their own corrections: quiet (doing nothing is being a bystander), notmean (only watching, not joining), join (laughing gives an audience), push and alone (you could get hurt, get a grown-up), wait (waiting lets someone get hurt), cared and notunkind (each waited for someone else), tales and business (telling keeps Mia safe). Sorter, crowd and scene taps also name the slip, e.g. tapping Mia in the crowd step.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores about grade -0.7 against the family kid limit of 5.0: short sentences, one-syllable words and named children (Zak is mean to Mia. Other kids see it.). Adult text scores 7.6 against the limit of 10 while using the precise terms passive bystander, upstander, target, audience, bystander effect, diffusion of responsibility and Relationships Education statutory guidance.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Each kid paragraph carries one idea (the three roles, doing nothing is a choice, be the first, safe help and telling); adult paragraphs give the curriculum duty, the key terms with research, four named mistakes with the safety rule, and the lab outline. Overlap with Understanding bullying and other lessons stays under the 12% gate.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android and iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: action cards wrap onto two lines instead of squeezing, the three role boxes sit in one row about 105 px wide, the crowd and six helper faces have names and thought labels that stay on screen, the five move tiles sit in a 2-2-1 grid, and the young-mode buttons below are at least 56 px tall. The risk pill uses dark text on the lighter dark-theme colours.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, and all five Show me tasks completed. Every canvas drag or tap has a labelled button twin (role buttons, 'Ben stops laughing', 'Ola helps first', 'Choose: Tell a grown-up', telling buttons) and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, e.g. '3 still laughing, so Zak still has an audience.'
